subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB254). The PARTIAL was leg a's UPPER half, defeated above 2**63 by the intake, not by the body. CITATIONS RE-DERIVED MECHANICALLY, none inherited: cite.py --check 15.90.4 "less than 16 010 000 or greater than 99 999 999" -> OK (15.90.4 1) a)); --check 15.90.4 "The year is not within the range 1601 to 9999" -> OK (1) a) NOTE 1); --check 15.90.4 "The date is valid" -> OK (1) d) NOTE 4); --check 15.90.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer" -> OK (15.90.3 rule 1); --check 15.3 "results in an incorrect value for that argument" -> OK (15.3 rule 14); --check 8.3.3.3.2 "fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits" -> OK. THE DERIVATION. 15.90.3 r1 is the WHOLE argument rule and constrains nothing but integer-ness; 15.90.4 r1a is a CATCH-ALL over both directions, so the function is TOTAL over the integers and every integer argument has a defined verdict. 15.3 rule 14 sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION only when evaluation 'results in an incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value according to the rules specified in the function definition' - there is no such value here, so a conforming program may pass any integer and must receive a verdict, never an abort. THE DEFECT, re-probed on this tree before the fix, not inherited from the note: (a) FLOAT lane - 01 FBIG USAGE COMP-2, COMPUTE FBIG = 1.0E19, FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(FBIG) printed 00, i.e. 1) d) 'The date is valid', where r1a requires 1; the body was CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#TestDateYyyymmddReal = 'TryIntegerArg(...) ? CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd(n) : 0' and the literal ': 0' tail is the verdict for VALID. (b) CHECKING-ON lane - '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' with 01 BIG19 PIC 9(19) VALUE 9999999999999999999 terminated the run unit: 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument 9999999999999999999 is outside the range the function can represent (ISO 15.3)' - on CONFORMING source. (c) NATIVE/Dec lane printed 01, the right code by COINCIDENCE ONLY: CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg substituted the checking-off default 0 for the ARGUMENT and 0 lands in the same r1a arm (0 < 16 010 000); the coincidence evaporates under checking, which is lane (b). THE FIX is at the validator, never at the shared narrowing: CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd now takes Int128 and answers r1a before any conversion (past the guard the value is eight digits, so the int narrowing is exact); IntrinsicRenderer's 'case "TestDateYyyymmdd" or "TestDayYyyyddd"' arm takes the WIDE intake IntArgWide -> AsIntWide, which has no raise point and, unlike AsInt, carries the U (UInt128) carrier arm as well; TestDateYyyymmddReal classifies by r1a on the VALUE, so +/-infinity and every magnitude past the window answer 1 without narrowing, and the one input that is the value of no integer (a NaN) routes to the shared 15.3 raise site and substitutes the documented implementor-defined result 1, never the 0 that would call a non-date a valid date. STRUCTURE, so the next case is automatic: the intake width is now derived from the runtime body's DECLARED carrier (Int128 = total, long = bounded), and IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests.EveryTotalIntegerArgument_TakesTheWideIntake re-derives that pairing by reflection and fails when an arm and its body disagree. The guard was proven RED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS on the shipped renderer before being trusted: reverting this arm produced 'TestDateYyyymmdd: body declares Int128 ... but the arm narrows' plus its sibling, and a stray widening of the DateOfInteger/DayOfInteger/IntegerOfDate/IntegerOfDay arm (whose 15.5.2 domain IS bounded, so the 15.3 landing is right there) produced the opposite four. THE GOLDEN that closes the row is conformance:cases/15.90.4-Returned-value-rule/pb254_total_integer_arguments, which pins r1a's UPPER half on every carrier an integer argument can arrive on - T1 100000000 -> 1; T2 99999999 -> 2, proving the bound is EXCLUSIVE and that r1a did not swallow the boundary (MOD(99999999 10000) = 9999 > 1299, so r1b fires); T3 a 19-digit LITERAL (8.3.3.3.2 requires 1..31 digits be accepted) -> 1; T4 a PIC 9(19) item -> 1; T5 a PIC 9(31) item -> 1; T6 the 15.3 type-6 arithmetic-expression witness P18 * 100 + 62 = 2**64 + 1 995 046 -> 1; T7 a FLOAT-LONG item holding 1.0E19 -> 1 - and it runs the whole program under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON with an ARMED CONTROL, because a checking-ON leg proves nothing if the directive is inert: leg ARMED raises the condition deliberately from FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY, whose 15.5.2 argument form IS bounded, and the USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative reports 'ARMED=EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION' before RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT leaves the receiver at its 99 preset. Every T value above was derived from the rule text first and then observed.
